Day 13/30 — Custom Compound Assignment Operators (.NET 10 & C# 14)

C# 14 introduces native support for custom compound assignment operators, letting us mutate readonly and value types in-place without generating intermediate heap allocations or defensive struct copies.

• **Memory Overhead:** Traditional binary operators instantiate new objects on every arithmetic step, triggering unnecessary Gen0 GC allocations.
• **In-Place Mutation:** Passing the left operand by reference allows direct register or stack mutation.
• **JIT Optimization:** The Roslyn compiler lowers compound assignments directly into optimized IL without hidden temporaries.

Watch out: Mutating readonly structs via ref requires careful handling to avoid unintended side effects across shared references.
